features.title: Manage hosts on a dedicated page
features.summary: The Hosts page lists registered machines in destination-picker order, shows live one-minute load and memory use, and lets users open or copy a temporary remote-host link. Users can add existing folders or clone Git repositories with optional individually selected local-file copying. Auto selects the eligible runtime with the lowest normalized resource pressure; hosts can be hidden, reordered, reconnected, edited, or removed, and SSH rows with runtime errors can be diagnosed hop by hop.
failureModes: A partial or duplicate order is refused and the stored order stays.
Diagnosis marks the failed SSH, runtime, or identity hop, shows its message and recovery path, and exposes a copyable report; request failures direct users to edit the SSH target or remote DSH home.
Hiding a host keeps its runtimes, threads and remote data; it only leaves the destination picker.
A local file-copy failure leaves the cloned repository registered and reports that the selected files were not copied.
Ignored files are not scanned unless explicitly requested; candidates are never selected automatically, and credential-like paths are blocked.
Remote host links use a temporary SSH tunnel and expire when their view lease closes.

features.title: Update every host from the Hosts page
features.summary: Update hosts checks every visible SSH host: it fetches the host repository and dry-runs that host's own dshx checkout sync, then lists what would change. Update all syncs each host that has changes (rebase onto main@origin, install, rebuild) and says per host whether DSH there needs a restart. Hosts are never restarted from here. Agents get the same operation as multi_host_update.
failureModes: A host without a built checkout, jj or an official Node build is reported with the provisioning step it needs.
A conflicted or refused sync leaves the host checkout as dshx checkout sync left it and names the recovery on that host.
Only commits on main@origin reach a host; local commits that are not pushed stay here.
A failed row keeps its error and offers Retry; other hosts continue.

verification.testName: reports rebuilt plugins and whether the host needs a restart
names what a machine lacks before it can update

verification.reason: A real update needs an SSH host with a built dshfiles checkout, which the browser journeys do not provision; the sync and failure handling are unit-tested and the dialog is reachable through its reach path.

features.title: Weight Auto placement and fetch before new threads
features.summary: Edit host sets an Auto weight (x1, x2, x4: Auto divides the host's resource pressure by it) and whether a thread started there first runs jj git fetch in its folder. A failed fetch never blocks the thread; the start result says why. Hiding a host also takes its threads out of the sidebar, and a remote thread whose host is unreachable offers Hide this host. A host that was online in the last 10 s reads as Reconnecting instead of turning red.
failureModes: A fetch that fails or times out (60 s) still starts the thread on what the host has.
Fetch only moves remote bookmarks; it never rebases a working copy on the host.

features.title: Delegate a task to another machine
features.summary: The multi_host_delegate agent tool runs a task as a thread on a named host, or on the least-loaded visible SSH host through Auto, waits for its turn and returns the final answer, like a subagent on that machine. A pending question on the host, a failed turn and a wait that runs out each come back with the thread id to follow; cancelling the call stops the remote turn.
failureModes: Auto with no visible SSH host that has fresh resource data refuses and names the recovery.
A question or approval on the host returns status waiting: only the host UI can answer it.
A wait that runs out returns status running with the sessionId; the remote turn keeps going.
Cancelling the tool call cancels the remote turn.

verification.testName: finishes with the last assistant text after the last prompt

verification.reason: An agent tool with no client surface; verified against two scratch DSHs, one registered as a local runtime of the other, where a delegated turn settled as failed with the remote status.

failureModes: Host-key or identity mismatch rejects attachment.
A missing or stale launch file reports runtime-not-running instead of connecting.

features.title: Use the native composer for remote threads
features.summary: The one-shot Auto destination selects the least-pressured visible remote host from fresh CPU and memory snapshots, then pins that runtime before folder selection; keep its model catalog, reasoning-effort picker, file attachments, and @ file references bound to the owning runtime, and follow/reply in the native chat.
failureModes: Auto skips hidden, stale, unsupported, or unreachable hosts and leaves the current destination unchanged when none is eligible.
A capability or version mismatch disables incompatible actions.
A file-reference request for an unowned Session or wrong runtime is refused before the remote filesystem is queried.
An unknown mutation result after a lost reply is inspected and never automatically replayed.
An @ mention under this Host's home, or an upload staged for another thread, is refused with a recovery message before it reaches the owning runtime; the composer keeps the draft.

externalDependencies.boundary: Token-authenticated HTTP/WebSocket RPC to a selected DSH runtime.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: Use an injected in-memory gateway transport with synthetic token and runtime identities; no real DSH profile credentials.

features.title: Answer a remote agent's questions and approvals in this client
features.summary: While a mirrored thread is followed, this Host opens the owning runtime's forwarded-event stream as an owner client, holds what the runtime waits on, and shows it in the native question card or an approval panel in the same seat. Answers go back to that runtime, which stays the authority; the first answer from any client wins and nothing is delegated away from the owner's own UI.
features.currentSurface: conversation composer seat of a mirrored thread
failureModes: A request the owner withdrew is refused here with a message to check the thread, and the card closes.
An answer the owner refuses stays a failed attempt on the card, and the request stays held.
A connection lost after an answer was sent reports an unknown outcome and is never retried automatically.
A runtime that refuses the wait claim keeps its own timer and the card shows no countdown.
A dropped event stream forgets what it held; the owner delivers it again on the next stream.
